note: A synthetic client (Slice 129 worked example). Not a real company.
problem: We are a regional grocery chain with 30 stores. We spend $1,200,000 a year on in-store promotions and cannot tell which ones pay off.

answers.common.decision: How to use our data to judge promotions; the commercial director decides which to keep.
answers.common.audience: The commercial director and our two data analysts.
answers.common.materials: We run about 400 promotions a year. Our loyalty card covers 65% of sales.
answers.consulting.current-state: We once held back 3 stores from a promotion to compare sales, but never repeated it. Promotions are planned on buyers' judgment.
answers.consulting.success: Know each promotion's sales lift soon after it ends, and cut spend on promotions that do not pay off by 20%.
answers.consulting.constraints: Our data team is two analysts; the loyalty data already sits in our data warehouse.
